title: OpenAI vs Apple text messages reveal something about Apple, but probably not what you’re thinking
excerpt: In the ongoing lawsuit between Apple and OpenAI, the ChatGPT parent just released messages and emails that paint a picture of something far more mundane than corporate espionage.
content_html:
We have officially reached the finger-pointing phase of the blockbuster Apple vs. OpenAI lawsuit in which Apple alleges that, with the assistance of former Apple employees, OpenAI is stealing Apple trade secrets.

What the suit alleges, which I outlined here, is pretty damning: A pair of former Apple employees — one a 25-year company veteran and another who spent a decade as an iPhone electrical engineer — allegedly held onto systems, asked OpenAI interviewees from Apple to share proprietary Apple info, and, Apple claims, told partners that sharing Apple's proprietary manufacturing information was okay with the Cupertino tech giant.

OpenAI quickly denied the allegations and, in short order, we learned that Apple's claims that it had contacted Lui Chang about the charges were incorrect because Apple's counsel had mixed up the names of Lui Chang with OpenAI's own counsel, Che Chang.

This week, however, OpenAI offered a more robust response, releasing a text chain between Lui Chang and a current unidentified Apple employee, and the email exchange in which it's revealed that Apple had been talking to the wrong Chang.

"Apple is one of the greatest companies of all time, and built a reputation for obsessing over the smallest details. This careless, aggressive and oddly personal lawsuit sadly doesn’t live up to that reputation," wrote OpenAI on its company blog on Monday.

A cry for help

What the messages appear to reveal is not corporate espionage, but something far more mundane and, in some ways, very relatable if you've ever worked at a large company.

I should preface this to say that Apple has not confirmed these messages, but it's hard to imagine OpenAI fabricating them. In fact, the sheer amount of redacted information gives more credence to their authenticity.

There's so much missing information that it might seem impossible to glean anything from the banter between "Apple Employee #1" and Chang, so, to help myself, I went through and inserted guesses about '[Redacted - Apple Information]" to try and make sense of the conversation. (I decided much of it was about the potential use of Silicon Carbon batteries in the upcoming iPhone 18.)

In the messages, the Apple employees seem to have worked with Chang and were not only missing him, but his expertise.

"Just in case you don’t have enough work, I need some help. I have a vague recollection of you talking about a [REDACTED]. Can you give me a brief refresh of this and point me to an EE who may have some knowledge?" wrote the Apple Employee. I'm assuming he's referring here to an "Electrical Engineer"

Without apparent hesitation, Chang replied, "I think what you referred to is [REDACTED]. And the small [REDACTED]." He then pointed the Apple Employee to someone else at Apple who "might still remember anything."

How about, just say no?

Now, Chang could've said, "Hey, dude, miss you, too, but I can't really talk about anything Apple-related anymore." According to this exchange, Chang did not and kept doing his best to help.

This Apple employee also seems unaware of best business practices and keeps talking about technology, at one point even mentioning a schematic. It looks like he also shared that schematic with Chang, but it may also have been Chang sharing the image with the Apple employee.

As the Apple Employee presses on, Chang tells him to look for a schematic in the "team box folder". He even mentions a "power block diagram." I'm a bit surprised that bit wasn't redacted.

One telling section from Chang jumped out at me, and this is the relatable part. As Chang kept trying to connect Apple Employee 1 to the expertise he required, Chang noted, "Now when I think about it. The other smart people also just left that team. The one that might still [be] in Apple is [Apple Employee #10]."

Brain drain is a real issue, it seems, even for Apple. So in addition to long-timer Chang leaving for OpenAI, others who seem to possess some important technical information have departed as well.

Later, as the quest for information continues, Chang recommended contacting a pair of Apple employees (#5 and #7).

At this point, there's a message that might've come from an automated system inside Apple's communication platform:

"Hi [Apple Employee #1 Name], [Apple Employee #3 Name], I can help get the conversation with [Apple Employee #6] and [Apple Employee #7] started."

Which led to my favorite part of the whole exchange. One of the Apple Employees auto-invited to the conversation essentially freaked out:

"Hi, this is highly irregular, please remove me from this thread."

Honestly, I feel for that person. As I've written before, Apple doesn't mess around when it comes to NDAs, proprietary information, or corporate secrets. Stumbling on a sort of illicit conversation about tech details between a current and former employee is surely enough to make any Apple employee hit the panic button.

Apple Employee #1 explains he added other employees "for awareness" but also shifts the conversation to an internal discussion. Chang is left to like the last message and, it seems, leaves it at that.

What's next?

The release of all this communication does not end the case. Far from it.

As of Monday evening, Apple filed with a US judge a strongly worded request for an injunction that, among other things, calls for "a preliminary injunction to stop the theft of its trade secrets.” It also includes the prediction, "Apple is likely to succeed on the merits of its trade secret claims."

Even so, I think this motion and the OpenAI post may move everything along toward an out-of-court settlement, one that would end the case but likely do little to repair this now-in-tatters Apple-OpenAI relationship.

In the end, though, OpenAI's post appears to reveal a mortal Apple, one that, despite its size and power, is still run by fallible humans who are often adrift, as any of us would be, when colleagues leave, taking with them friendship and, more importantly, knowledge.

Apple is building complex products, and corporate memory is a critical part of the process (so much so that incoming CEO John Ternus apparently just rehired a retired Apple hardware executive).

Understanding when, how, and why decisions were made and how they could impact future projects is invaluable. Sometimes, only those who were in the room know the truth of the matter. Chang, it appears, was one of those people. He had the information, took it with him, and now, it seems, someone wanted to keep the lines of communication open, which is exactly what Apple doesn't want.

content_html_zh:
我们正式进入了轰动一时的苹果与 OpenAI 诉讼的相互指责阶段，苹果声称 OpenAI 在前苹果员工的帮助下窃取了苹果的商业机密。

我在这里概述的诉讼指控非常令人震惊：两名前苹果员工——其中一名是在公司工作了 25 年的老员工，另一名是 iPhone 电气工程师，有 10 年的时间——据称掌握着系统，要求苹果的 OpenAI 受访者分享苹果的专有信息，并且苹果声称，他们告诉合作伙伴，这家库比蒂诺科技巨头可以分享苹果的专有制造信息。

OpenAI 很快否认了这些指控，很快我们就了解到，苹果公司关于其已就这些指控与 Lui Chang 联系的说法是不正确的，因为苹果公司的律师将 Lui Chang 的名字与 OpenAI 自己的律师 Che Chang 的名字混淆了。

然而，本周，OpenAI 做出了更强有力的回应，发布了 Lui Chang 和一名身份不明的苹果现任员工之间的文本链，以及显示苹果一直在与错误的 Chang 交谈的电子邮件往来。

“苹果是有史以来最伟大的公司之一，并以注重细节而闻名。 遗憾的是，这场粗心、咄咄逼人且奇怪的个人诉讼并没有名副其实。”OpenAI 周一在其公司博客上写道。

呼救声

这些信息似乎揭示的并不是企业间谍活动，而是一些更为平常的事情，而且在某些方面，如果你曾经在一家大公司工作过，那么这些信息会非常引起你的共鸣。

我应该在序言中指出，苹果尚未证实这些消息，但很难想象 OpenAI 会捏造它们。 事实上，大量经过编辑的信息更能证明其真实性。

订阅突发新闻、评论、观点、顶级技术交易等。

缺失的信息太多，似乎不可能从“Apple 员工 #1”和 Chang 之间的玩笑中收集到任何信息，因此，为了帮助自己，我浏览并插入了有关“[已编辑 - Apple 信息]”的猜测，以尝试理解对话。 （我认为这主要是关于即将推出的 iPhone 18 中碳硅电池的潜在用途。）

在这些信息中，苹果员工似乎曾与张共事过，他们不仅想念他，还想念他的专业知识。

“以防万一你的工作不够，我需要一些帮助。 我依稀记得你谈论过[已编辑]。 您能给我简单介绍一下这一点，并为我指点一位可能有一些知识的 EE 吗？” 苹果员工写道。 我假设他在这里指的是“电气工程师”

张毫不犹豫地回答道：“我认为你指的是[已编辑]。 还有小的[已编辑]。” 然后，他向这位苹果员工推荐了苹果公司的其他人，“可能还记得任何事情”。

直接说不怎么样？

现在，张可以说：“嘿，伙计，我也想你，但我不能再谈论任何与苹果有关的事情了。” 根据这次交流，张没有并继续尽力提供帮助。

这位苹果员工似乎也不了解最佳商业实践，并且一直在谈论技术，甚至一度提到了原理图。 看起来他也与 Chang 分享了该示意图，但也可能是 Chang 与 Apple 员工分享了该图像。

当苹果员工继续追问时，Chang 告诉他在“团队文件夹”中查找原理图。 他甚至提到了“电源框图”。 我有点惊讶，那部分内容没有被编辑。

张的一个讲述性的部分让我印象深刻，这就是相关的部分。 当 Chang 不断尝试将 Apple 员工 1 与他所需的专业知识联系起来时，Chang 指出：“现在当我想到这一点时。 其他聪明人也刚刚离开了这个团队。 可能仍留在苹果的人是[苹果员工#10]。”

看来，即使对于苹果来说，人才流失也是一个现实问题。 因此，除了张先生离开 OpenAI 之外，其他似乎拥有一些重要技术信息的人也离开了。

后来，随着继续寻找信息，Chang 建议联系两名 Apple 员工（#5 和 #7）。

此时，有一条消息可能来自苹果通信平台内的自动化系统：

“嗨，[Apple 员工 #1 姓名]，[Apple 员工 #3 姓名]，我可以帮助您开始与 [Apple 员工 #6] 和 [Apple 员工 #7] 的对话。”

这导致了整个交流中我最喜欢的部分。 一位自动邀请参加对话的苹果员工基本上吓坏了：

“嗨，这是非常不正常的，请把我从这个帖子中删除。”

老实说，我对那个人有感觉。 正如我之前所写，苹果在保密协议、专有信息或公司机密方面不会乱七八糟。 无意中发现现任和前任员工之间有关技术细节的非法对话肯定足以让任何苹果员工感到恐慌。

Apple 员工＃1 解释说，他添加了其他员工“是为了提高认识”，但也将对话转变为内部讨论。 张留下了对最后一条信息的点赞，并且似乎就这样了。

接下来怎么办？

所有这些通讯的发布并没有结束此案。 远非如此。

截至周一晚间，苹果公司向美国法官提交了一份措辞强硬的禁令请求，其中包括“发布初步禁令，制止窃取其商业机密的行为”。 它还包括这样的预测：“苹果很可能因其商业秘密主张而获得成功。”

即便如此，我认为这项动议和 OpenAI 的帖子可能会推动一切朝着庭外和解的方向发展，这将结束此案，但可能对修复现在已经支离破碎的 Apple-OpenAI 关系无济于事。

不过，最终，OpenAI 的帖子似乎揭示了一个凡人的苹果，尽管它规模庞大、实力雄厚，但其运营者仍然是容易犯错的人，这些人经常随波逐流，就像我们任何人一样，当同事离开时，他们带走了友谊，更重要的是，知识。

苹果正在打造复杂的产品，而企业内存是这个过程的关键部分（以至于即将上任的首席执行官约翰·特努斯显然只是重新雇用了一位退休的苹果硬件高管）。

了解决策的时间、方式和原因以及它们如何影响未来的项目是非常宝贵的。 有时候，事情的真相，只有在场的人才知道。 张看来就是其中之一。 他掌握了这些信息，并随身携带，而现在，似乎有人想要保持沟通渠道的畅通，而这正是苹果所不希望的。

兰斯是一位拥有 38 年行业经验的资深人士和屡获殊荣的记者，自从个人电脑只有手提箱大小而“在线”意味着“等待”以来，他一直在报道技术。 他曾担任 Lifewire 的主编、Mashable 的主编，此前还担任过 PCMag.com 的主编和 Ziff Davis, Inc. 的内容高级副总裁。他还为 Medium 撰写了一篇颇受欢迎的每周科技专栏，名为“The Upgrade”。
